name: Sofia Carvalho
life_context: UX designer at a startup. Worked 70-hour weeks for 2.5 years, cancelled all social plans, gradually lost her social circle. Now 3 months into therapy, starting to recover.

psychographic.social_style: Wants to reconnect but fears falling back into overwork mode. Needs structured, time-boxed social activities.

motivations: rebuild friendships lost during burnout
relearn how to have fun without guilt
find activities that don't feel like networking
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Meetup groups were too output-oriented
Everything felt like networking, not connection
No app understood WHY she stopped socializing
expectations: App that understands burnout context
Low commitment options
No performance pressure

name: Daniel Kim
city: São Paulo, Brazil (Korean expat, 8 months in SP)
life_context: QA engineer at a Brazilian fintech. Speaks intermediate Portuguese. Lives alone. Colleagues are friendly but he hasn't built real friendships yet.

psychographic.social_style: Struggles with language barrier in social settings. Prefers structured activities where language is secondary.

motivations: make friends outside of work
practice Portuguese in a low-stakes setting
find Korean or Asian community events
frustrations_with_previous_apps: InterNations is for older expats
Tandem only for language exchange, gets romantic
Language barrier makes casual social apps unusable
expectations: International/multilingual community
Activity-first so language is not the only thing they share
English option in the app

name: Beatriz Santos
life_context: HR manager, divorced 8 months ago after a 10-year marriage. Single mother of a 7-year-old daughter. Social circle was mostly couples-based and has largely disappeared.

psychographic.social_style: Wants to rebuild adult social life but is constrained by parenting schedule. Most free time is during non-peak hours.

motivations: find other divorced parents for solidarity
rediscover who she is outside of being a wife
find family-friendly activities for weekends with her daughter
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Dating apps feel too soon
Friend apps feel juvenile
No app recognizes she needs both adult social time AND mother-daughter activities
expectations: Family-friendly event options clearly surfaced
Events at reasonable hours (not 10pm bar nights)
Privacy — doesn't want divorce details to be visible to strangers

name: Rafael Martins
life_context: Former investment banker, recently transitioned to photography full-time. Has a wide professional network but few true friends. Moved to Rio from SP 2 years ago.

psychographic.social_style: Comfortable socially but finds most events superficial. Wants depth, not volume.

motivations: find photographer community
build friendships based on shared passion, not career
prove to himself that life after corporate can be richer
frustrations_with_previous_apps: LinkedIn is the wrong vibe
Instagram DMs feel cold
Most social apps feel like they're for 22-year-olds in crisis
expectations: Adult, thoughtful community
Events that reward showing up repeatedly (not just one-offs)
App that helps him feel like part of a scene, not just a calendar

name: Emma Johansson
city: São Paulo, Brazil (Swedish, on 6-month work assignment)
life_context: Product manager at a Swedish company's SP office. Highly functional, multilingual, but genuinely lonely in a new country where social norms feel foreign.

psychographic.social_style: Prefers small groups, structured activities, getting to know people over time. Uncomfortable with the Brazilian social expectation of instant warmth.

motivations: build a real social life in Brazil, not just expat bubble
understand Brazilian culture from the inside
have friends to call when the work assignment gets hard
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Internations feels like a corporate networking event
Language barrier even for a fluent Portuguese speaker (cultural nuance)
All apps assume you're there long-term — no grace for temporary residents
expectations: English UI option (exists in Reroot ✓)
Small group format
Culturally diverse events, not just generic gatherings

name: André Oliveira
life_context: Software developer. Lost his closest friend to suicide 10 months ago. Has been in grief therapy. Ready to start reconnecting but social setbacks feel enormous.

psychographic.social_style: Cannot do forced positivity. Needs spaces where showing up quietly is enough.

motivations: honor his friend by rebuilding life
find a community of people who don't expect constant happiness
be around people without having to explain the grief
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Everything is engineered around fun, FOMO, excitement
No app understands 'I want to be around people without talking much'
Social media is actively harmful right now
expectations: Low-pressure attendance model
App that doesn't punish you for going quiet
Feels like it was built for humans, not engagement metrics

name: Clara Zhang
city: São Paulo, Brazil (Chinese, 1 year in Brazil)
life_context: International trade analyst at a Chinese export company. Portuguese is functional but not fluent. Has a tight-knit Chinese expat circle but wants to expand beyond it.

psychographic.social_style: Comfortable one-on-one, nervous in large groups where she might miss cultural references.

motivations: make Brazilian friends (not just expat connections)
improve Portuguese through real interaction
feel like she belongs in SP, not just works there
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Most events assume native-level cultural fluency
Hard to find non-alcohol-centric social settings
Bilingual events are rare
expectations: Small group events where she won't get lost
Activity-based so language is secondary
Visual, clear UI (language barrier applies to app itself)

name: Marcos Pereira
life_context: Just retired from 25 years as a civil engineer. Wife still working. Realizes his entire social identity was job-related and has collapsed now that he's retired.

psychographic.social_style: Used to being in charge. Needs social settings with clear roles and activities.

motivations: fill the social void left by retirement
find men his age to have real conversations with
stay mentally active and connected
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Apps feel designed for young people in crises he doesn't relate to
Registration is confusing
Events are for evenings — he's free during the day
expectations: Daytime events
Simple, clear navigation
Community of people at similar life stages

name: Isabela Costa
life_context: 3rd year architecture student. Lives with roommates but feels isolated — everyone is exhausted and stressed. Online friends feel more real than university ones.

psychographic.social_style: Freezes in unstructured social settings. Needs activities with clear entry points.

motivations: meet people outside of architecture bubble
prove to herself she can have a social life
find creative communities (art, design, writing)
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Bumble BFF felt like forced friendships
Eventbrite events are too large and impersonal
Social anxiety means most social apps make things worse
expectations: Icebreaker-structured activities
No penalty for not talking (activity provides cover)
Option to get to know events before committing

name: Tomás Herrera
city: São Paulo, Brazil (Argentine expat, 3 years in SP)
life_context: Senior product manager at a Brazilian tech company. Has SP settled — apartment, job, partner — but his social circle is still thin. Wants a friend group he chose, not defaulted into.

traits: gets bored easily with shallow connections
psychographic.social_style: Makes friends easily but has trouble finding depth. Doesn't want surface-level social.

motivations: intentionally build a friend group (not just work colleagues)
find intellectual and physical activities (cycling, debates)
have the social life in SP that he planned but delayed
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Meetup groups feel superficial and corporate
Friend-finding apps feel awkward for someone already socially confident
No app rewards showing up repeatedly to become a regular
expectations: Recurring event support or at least regulars/community aspect
Events that scale into friendship, not just one-offs
Spontaneous options for his impulsive side

name: Juliana Ramos
life_context: Teacher, divorced, two teenagers. Her social circle is mostly former couples friends who drifted away. Skeptical of technology and social apps after a bad experience on a dating site.

psychographic.social_style: Needs to build trust slowly. Won't engage with anything that feels 'expose-y' or linked to dating.

motivations: rebuild social life without it being mistaken for dating
find adult women communities (book clubs, cooking classes)
feel normal and not judged for her situation
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Everything eventually feels like it's trying to get you to date
Location data feels invasive
Complex apps feel risky — she doesn't trust she won't accidentally share something
expectations: Clear separation from dating apps in branding and UX
Privacy-first by default, not opt-in
Simple enough that she can figure it out herself

name: Kwame Asante
city: São Paulo, Brazil (Ghanaian expat, 14 months in SP)
life_context: Data engineer at a startup, highly sociable, has built some connections but misses the spontaneous social culture he had in Accra. Everything in SP requires scheduling 2 weeks in advance.

psychographic.social_style: Initiates social plans. Loves large groups and spontaneous gatherings. Gets restless with over-planned events.

motivations: replicate the spontaneous social culture of Accra in SP
find a diverse social circle
become someone who knows SP nightlife and daily rhythm deeply
frustrations_with_previous_apps: Everything requires booking days ahead
Events list is the same 10 things every week
No way to see what's happening RIGHT NOW
expectations: Real-time or same-day event discovery
High-energy community events, not just introverted activities
Group coordination tools — he always brings people along
